title: Platform: SDK stubs, host/iOS builds, the VideoToolbox plug-in shim, logging
state: host-tested (Linux x86-64, ASan+UBSan and TSan) and compiled+linked for arm64-apple-ios16.0; nothing was installed or run on the phone
done: sdk/sysinc: 20 hand-written freestanding headers (sys/types, stdio, stdlib, string, pthread, unistd, fcntl, dlfcn, time, sys/time, mach/mach_time, errno, sys/wait, signal, math, assert, dirent, sys/stat, sys/utsname, poll). Darwin ABI sizes: pthread_mutex_t 64, pthread_cond_t 48, pthread_once_t 16, struct dirent 1048, mode_t 16-bit, dev_t 32-bit; Darwin flag values: O_NONBLOCK 4, O_NOCTTY 0x20000, RTLD_NOW 2, RTLD_LOCAL 4. Every header is self-contained and compiles on its own with -ffreestanding -nostdinc (20/20 in the suite).

sdk/make_tbds.py: reads gpu/video/*/symbols.txt, gpu/video/*/*/symbols.txt and sdk/symbols.txt; folds /usr/lib/system/libsystem_* and /usr/lib/libsystem_* owners into /usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib; writes one tbd v4 (targets [arm64-ios]) per install name into sdk/lib; fails on a symbol listed twice with different owners and on an owner with no INFO entry, and writes nothing in either error case; idempotent (a second run reports '0 file(s) changed'); removes stale TBDs.

sdk/symbols.txt: the platform package's own imports (libSystem incl. ___error, CoreFoundation incl. ___CFConstantStringClassReference and _kCFAllocatorDefault, VideoToolbox), plus make_tbds.py's BASELINE of compiler-emitted libSystem symbols (memcpy/memset/.../__stack_chk_*) so a plain C package cannot forget them.

vt/n2vt_log.h/.c: n2vt_say() writes 'N2VIDEO <progname>[pid]: <text>\n' to /dev/console, opening and closing it per line with Darwin O_WRONLY|O_NONBLOCK|O_NOCTTY (values checked against <fcntl.h> at compile time on the phone build); 40 lines per process then exactly one '(further lines suppressed)' line; silent when N2VT_SWITCH_QUIET exists; mutex-protected; write errors and a missing console are ignored; 480-byte line buffer, truncation safe.

vt/n2vt_shim.c: the plug-in; exports exactly SLIMEncoderRegister and n2vt_version (the latter returns 1). Body once per process via pthread_once: N2VT_SWITCH_OFF -> one 'off' line and return; VTRegisterVideoEncoderWithInfo NULL -> one line and return; HEVC (Apple's HEVCVideoEncoder_CreateInstance out of VCPHEVC.videocodec via dlopen(RTLD_NOW|RTLD_LOCAL)+dlsym) registered for hvc1 and hev1 with CMClassImplementationID = N2VT_ID_HEVC; avc1 via the weak n2avc_vt_create with N2VT_ID_AVC; jpeg via the weak n2jpeg_vt_create with N2VT_ID_JPEG; each unless its N2VT_SWITCH_NO_* file exists; N2VT_SWITCH_CLAIM_HW adds kVTVideoEncoder_IsHardwareAccelerated = kCFBooleanTrue; one summary line with ok/failed/off/absent per codec type. Every CoreFoundation/VideoToolbox symbol is a weak import and is checked before use; the two encoder factories are weak imports (linker -U while their package is absent). No threads, no retained allocation, no dlclose (the factory must stay valid).

build_ios.sh [outdir]: runs make_tbds.py, compiles vt/*.c (leaving out vt/n2avc_vt.c while avc/*.c is absent, the documented stage-0 v0 plug-in), avc/*.c, jpeg/*.c and -- only when avc/*.c exists, because they exist for the encoder -- kern/n2vk_ref.c and kern/n2vk_dispatch.c, with the flags of PLAN.md 4.3; links Slim.videoencoder (-dylib, -install_name /System/Library/VideoEncoders/Slim.videoencoder, -adhoc_codesign, -exported_symbol for exactly the two exports, libSystem+CoreFoundation normal and every other TBD weak); checks file(1), the dylib id, the exact export list and that every undefined symbol is covered by a TBD. Then links n2vt_probe from probe/*.c (+ probe/av/*.c, or -DPROBE_NO_AV automatically when probe/av/ has no sources, or on PROBE_NO_AV=1) as a main executable, with the same symbol-coverage check. Prints sha256 and size of each product.
build_host.sh [package] and run_all_tests.sh: every <pkg>/run_tests.sh and <pkg>/<sub>/run_tests.sh, each last line and a total, exit 1 if any failed; LC_ALL=C for stable order.

vt/test/t_shim.c + run_tests.sh + this STATUS.json: 11 shim/log checks in four binaries (full matrix ASan+UBSan; no-avc-factory; no-VT-register; 4 threads x 3 calls under TSan) plus the 20-header self-containment check. The CoreFoundation subset used by the shim is a local fake in the test file; access/dlopen/dlsym/open/write/close/getpid/getprogname/VTRegisterVideoEncoderWithInfo are test doubles, and the test asserts the literal Darwin arguments (paths, RTLD flags, open flags, codec types, implementation IDs, the IsHardwareAccelerated key, registration order).

build_ios.sh links every non-libSystem/CoreFoundation framework with -weak_library and passes -dead_strip_dylibs: the plug-in's load commands are exactly libSystem + CoreFoundation (normal) + VideoToolbox (weak), and llvm-objdump --macho --dyld-info shows _n2avc_vt_create and _n2jpeg_vt_create as 'flat-namespace ... (weak import)' while every CoreFoundation and VideoToolbox symbol is a '(weak import)' bound to its named image.

The ad-hoc code signatures were parsed: both products carry one CodeDirectory (version 0x20400, flags 0x20002 = CS_ADHOC|CS_LINKER_SIGNED, hashType 2 = SHA-256, hashSize 32, pageSize 4096) and every page hash matches (17/17 for the plug-in, 24/24 for the probe). That is a structurally valid ad-hoc signature; arm64 dyld accepts that class for non-platform binaries (the C1 answer will be whether the specific path/process policy does).
not_done: No phone work of any kind: nothing was installed, no cycle was run, no console line has ever been produced by the device. 'Compiled and linked for iOS' is the strongest claim this package makes.

The plug-in was never loaded by a real VideoToolbox: whether dyld in mediaserverd/CMPhoto's host accepts an ad-hoc-signed dylib at /System/Library/VideoEncoders/Slim.videoencoder, and whether VTLoadVideoEncoders reaches that path, is cycle C1's question.

In this tree the avc1 registration could not be link-tested with the real encoder: avc/*.c did not exist when this was written, so build_ios.sh leaves vt/n2avc_vt.c out and the plug-in registers HEVC only. vt/n2avc_vt.c did compile for iOS before that rule was added; when WP03 lands, build_ios.sh includes it automatically and the same export/undefined-symbol checks run. The 'avc1 registered' path itself is host-tested with a fake factory.
The jpeg path has never been built with n2jpeg_vt_create present (the reserve package R1); only the 'absent' branch is exercised.
sysinc has no struct stat, no termios, no netinet, no CoreFoundation/Objective-C headers: nothing in gpu/video needs them yet. Ask on the board and they are added.

make_tbds.py's current-version/compatibility-version numbers for frameworks are metadata only (the linker uses the install name); they were not read out of the phone's cache. The LEAD verifies every symbol name against the cache's export tries.
The probe link currently exercises the -DPROBE_NO_AV path because probe/av/ was empty at the time of writing; the full link (with WP06's sources) has not been run from this package.

kern/n2vk_dispatch.c (WP08) does not compile for iOS as it stands: it calls snprintf without <stdio.h>. Because of that (and because nothing in the stage-0 plug-in calls the kernels) build_ios.sh keeps kern/*.c out of the link until avc/*.c exists; it was reported to WP08. The 'avc present' link path itself was checked in a scratch copy with a stub avc/*.c: the plug-in linked (72880 B, 74 undefined symbols all covered, still exactly two exports), so the rule works and the only outstanding blocker for the avc1-capable plug-in is the real avc/*.c plus that include fix.

probe/av/probe_av.c (WP06) does not compile for iOS as it stands (missing <stdio.h> for snprintf/vsnprintf and 13 Class-vs-id pointer errors); reported to WP06. With probe/av/ present the default build_ios.sh therefore exits 1 at the probe compile, after the plug-in has been built and checked. 'PROBE_NO_AV=1 bash build_ios.sh' builds everything C1 needs (probe without the AV tests); a bug in that flag (probe/av/*.c was still compiled) was found and fixed.

known_risks: Info-dictionary ownership: the shim passes a freshly created CFDictionary to VTRegisterVideoEncoderWithInfo and releases it immediately after both HEVC registrations ('no allocation kept'). This assumes VideoToolbox copies or retains the dictionary, as CF's Create/Copy/Get naming rules imply for an API that keeps its argument. If it stored a bare pointer, the registry would later read freed memory. If the lead prefers belt-and-braces, keeping the dictionary alive (one small leak per process) is a one-line change.

kVTVideoEncoder_IsHardwareAccelerated is read as a value and only after VTRegisterVideoEncoderWithInfo was found: both come from VideoToolbox, so the read cannot happen with the image unloaded. The availability check for the data symbol would be '&symbol != NULL', which the current code does not use because the value is what is needed.

The weak-import link behaviour was verified with ld64.lld 23.1.4 (a dylib with -U for the two absent factories, and a dylib with the factory defined in a hidden-visibility object), not with Apple's ld64; the resulting Mach-O carries a weak undefined reference and no text relocation.

pthread_once semantics under fork: each forked test child inherits 'once not run', which is what the scenarios rely on. On the phone the plug-in is registered by VideoToolbox once per process; nothing in the shim forks.
The console budget is per process, not per encoding session: a long-lived mediaserverd that loads the plug-in once gets those 40 lines for its whole life (the design in n2vt_log.h).

sdk/sysinc/stdio.h declares FILE as struct __sFILE (opaque); the probe only passes FILE* around, never inspects it. A package that needs stdin/stdout buffering internals would need a different solution.
struct tm and struct utsname are hand-written from the Darwin ABI; the probe writes into their fields (gmtime_r, uname). A wrong field offset would be caught only on the phone (C1).

The probe executable is ad-hoc signed by ld64.lld; whether the phone's launchd/AMFI loads an ad-hoc-signed executable from /usr/libexec is a C1 question (the camera bundle's precedent says yes for dylibs).

The plug-in's object set follows the tree: vt/n2avc_vt.c is in the link only when avc/*.c exists, and kern/n2vk_{ref,dispatch}.c only then too. That keeps the stage-0 payload buildable, but it also means 'the plug-in built' must always be read together with the source list build_ios.sh prints.
